experiment: Experiment 0: host-mediated name resolution from Sandhi contracts
scope: nix/sandhi/docs/DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-05 (experiment 0 implementation scope), recorded at ca885b9 before the test existed

recorder.runtime: Claude Code remote session started by Mora

builder.note: QEMU software emulation; the test sets requiredFeatures.kvm = false

output.driverLog: driver.log (test-driver lines only; guest console lines omitted)

observed.guestNameService: nsncd 1.5.2; socket /run/nscd/socket mode srwxrwxrwx owned by nscd; /var/run/nscd/socket resolves to it; hosts: mymachines files myhostname dns; resolv.conf nameserver 127.0.0.4 only
observed.empty: No network (PrivateNetwork=yes, AF_UNIX only). getaddrinfo resolved the contract-chosen name to 127.0.0.9. The upstream logged that exact name from 127.0.0.1. The direct query failed with EAFNOSUPPORT and was not logged.
observed.networked: Peer 127.0.0.2 only. getaddrinfo resolved the contract-chosen name. The upstream logged it from 127.0.0.1. The direct query to 127.0.0.4 failed with EPERM and was not logged. The declared peer was reachable.
observed.emptyBlocked: Same as empty, plus InaccessiblePaths=/run/nscd. The socket was not visible (EACCES). getaddrinfo failed (EAI_NONAME). The upstream logged nothing.
observed.networkedBlocked: Same as networked, plus InaccessiblePaths=/run/nscd. The socket was not visible. getaddrinfo failed (EAI_AGAIN); its in-process DNS fallback was stopped by the IP filter. The upstream logged nothing. The declared peer was reachable.

findings.hostMediatedResolution: Demonstrated, in this guest, for both an empty-recipient and a networked contract.
findings.outboundChannel: Demonstrated, in this guest. A query name generated inside each contract reached an upstream resolver that the contract's own network controls do not admit. The host name-service daemon sent the query, so the contract's IP filter never saw it. Capacity and rate were not measured.
findings.socketBlockedComparison: With /run/nscd inaccessible, neither contract resolved the name and the upstream logged neither name. This was a test-local override. Its effect on other lookups that use the same socket, such as user and group names, was not measured.

limits: One disposable guest, one NSS configuration (nsncd; no systemd-resolved), one attempt. Other hosts may expose other resolver sockets, for example systemd-resolved's.

The upstream was a fixture inside the guest. On a real host the daemon forwards to whatever resolver the host is configured with, which may be off-host. That is inferred from configuration, not measured here.
No mitigation is adopted. No module code changed. Nothing here is a production claim.
The six existing checks were not rerun for this experiment.
